'''Marie-Paule Malliavin''', née ''Brameret'', (1935 in [[Mahdia]] – 25 September 2019 in Paris)<ref>{{Cite web |title=matchID – Moteur de recherche des décès |url=https://deces.matchid.io/id/zFBda3qunrST |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007194513/https://deces.matchid.io/id/zFBda3qunrST |url-status=live }}</ref> was a French mathematician who specialised in the field of algebra.<ref name="data_bnf_fr">{{Cite web |title=Marie-Paule Malliavin (BnF data) |url=https://data.bnf.fr/en/12283522/marie-paule_malliavin/#about |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007194433/https://data.bnf.fr/en/12283522/marie-paule_malliavin/#about |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Family==
She was married to the mathematician [[Paul Malliavin]] since 27 April 1965. They had two children (Thérèse and Marie-Joseph).<ref name="whoiswho_fr_paul">{{Cite web |title=Biographie Paul Malliavin Universitaire, Membre de l´Institut. |url=https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-paul-malliavin_15978 |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-06-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619115925/https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-paul-malliavin_15978 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==

She published her first mathematical article in 1960<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie-Paule Malliavin – Author Profile – zbMATH Open |url=https://zbmath.org/authors/malliavin.marie-paule |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-10-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007194443/https://zbmath.org/authors/malliavin.marie-paule |url-status=live }}</ref> and received her doctorate in 1965.<ref name="kosmann_schwarzbach">{{Cite arXiv|eprint=1502.07597 |last1=Kosmann-Schwarzbach |first1=Yvette |title=Women mathematicians in France in the mid-twentieth century |date=2015 |class=math.HO }}</ref>

After her doctorate, she first became maître de conférences at the [[University of Caen Normandy|University of Caen]].<ref name="nachruf">{{Cite web |title=» Anciennes actualités – section: Marie-Paule Malliavin (1935–2019) |url=https://www.imj-prg.fr/blog/2020/10/21/anciennes-actualites/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-01-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129125801/https://www.imj-prg.fr/blog/2020/10/21/anciennes-actualites/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Later she became a professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (UPMC, Paris 6) in Paris, where she remained until her retirement.<ref name="kosmann_schwarzbach" /><ref name="nachruf" />

Her mathematical students include Jacques Alev and Youssef El From.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie-Paule Malliavin – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=103205 |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2022-09-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915180656/https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=103205 |url-status=live }}</ref> She wrote several textbooks; the books on commutative algebra and representation theory of finite groups are frequently cited.<ref name="nachruf" />

At the beginning of her career, she worked on [[commutative algebra]], later on [[non-commutative algebra]]. This was at a time when [[Enveloping algebra (disambiguation)|enveloping algebras]] and then [[quantum group]]s were evolving. She collaborated with her husband Paul Malliavin in particular in the study of [[Haar measure|measures]] on infinite-dimensional groups.<ref name="nachruf" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering Paul Malliavin |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400568p.pdf |access-date=2023-10-03 |archive-date=2023-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230627061841/https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400568p.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

Marie-Paule Malliavin was editor of top-ranked international research journals.<ref name="nachruf" /> She also organised the Algebra Seminar at the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] for several decades, succeeding the deceased Professor [[Paul Dubreil]].<ref name="nachruf" />
